title: Self-energy pole optimization of superconductivity in the bilayer Hubbard model
authors: Taka-Shi Fujiwara, Shiro Sakai, Ryotaro Arita
abstract: We study the real-frequency structure of the self-energy in the bilayer Hubbard model, using the dynamical cluster approximation. At half filling, the Mott insulator-band insulator (MI-BI) crossover involves a rearrangement of self-energy poles between the bonding and antibonding bands; these poles cross as the interlayer hopping $t_{\perp}$ is varied. Upon doping, this pole structure produces a band-selective pseudogap and enhances $s^{\pm}$-wave superconductivity. The order parameter is maximized near the MI-BI boundary, where low-energy anomalous self-energy poles develop simultaneously in both bands and cooperatively enhance the pairing. We further show that these self-energy poles can be interpreted as emergent fermionic excitations, offering an enhanced-pairing mechanism in common with the single-layer Hubbard model. The controllability of these poles through $t_{\perp}$ makes the bilayer system an unconventional platform for optimizing strongly correlated superconductivity.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the bilayer Hubbard model, showing that superconducting pairing is optimally enhanced near a Mott Insulator–Band Insulator crossover. This enhancement mechanism is driven by the cooperative development of low-energy self-energy poles in both electronic bands. The work demonstrates that interlayer hopping ($t_\perp$) acts as a tunable knob to control this exotic pairing mechanism.
main_problem: The study investigates how the real-frequency structure of the self-energy dictates superconductivity enhancement in the bilayer Hubbard model.
main_result: Superconductivity is maximized near the Mott Insulator–Band Insulator (MI–BI) crossover boundary, where low-energy self-energy poles from both bands cooperatively enhance $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing.
method: The research employs the Dynamical Cluster Approximation (DCA) combined with an equation of motion approach to analyze spectral functions and self-energies.
model_or_system: The system is the bilayer Hubbard model on a square lattice, described by hopping parameters ($t, t_\perp$) and onsite repulsion ($U$). The analysis focuses on bonding ($ eta$) and antibonding ($\alpha$) bands.
key_observables: Self-energy poles (real-frequency structure), superconducting order parameter ($\Delta$), band-selective pseudogaps, and the excitation gap $\Delta$.
important_parameters: Interlayer hopping ($t_\perp$), onsite repulsion ($U$), doping level ($\delta=0.02$ to $0.05$), and the MI–BI crossover boundary.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on interpreting self-energies via a 'hidden-fermion model' which successfully captures pole structure across the crossover, although this ansatz fails at higher doping levels.
figures_summary: Figures map out superconducting order parameters in $(U, t_\perp)$ planes, showing maxima near the MI–BI boundary. Other figures illustrate spectral functions and self-energy evolution during the MI–BI crossover via pole crossing.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the self-energy poles across doping regimes ($\delta=0$ to $\delta=0.05$) and varying $t_\perp$. It first establishes the MI–BI crossover mechanism, then uses this structure to explain enhanced pairing, culminating in mapping out phase boundaries.
why_interesting: The concept of using controllable parameters ($t_\perp$) to tune emergent fermionic excitations (self-energy poles) for optimizing superconductivity is highly relevant to understanding engineered quantum materials and strongly correlated physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Spectral function Aγ(K, ω) (top row) and imaginary part of the normal self-energy Im Σnor γ (K, ω) (bottom row) at half filling (δ = 0) and U = 12 for t⊥= 0, 1.0, 1.62, 2.0, and 3.0 (left to right). Red and blue curves denote the Γ-α and M-β components; the black curve in the top row is the total DOS. The poles of Im Σnor γ , located inside the Mott gap, cross around t⊥≃t⊥,c ≃1.62, identifying the MI–BI crossover as a rearrangement of these poles between the two components. Insets in the lower panels show the bare (U = 0) band dispersions εγ(k) along Γ-X-M-Γ.

FIG. 2. Superconducting order parameters in the (U, t⊥) plane at δ = 0.02: ⟨cα Γ↑cα Γ↓⟩for the Γ-α component (left) and ⟨cβ M↑cβ M↓⟩for the M-β component (right), on a common color scale. The opposite signs (Γ-α < 0: blue, M-β > 0: red) indicate s±-wave symmetry. The phase diagram at half filling is superimposed (M: metal, MI: Mott insulator, BI: band in- sulator; the MI–BI boundary is determined in Sec. S5). Both components are largest near the MI–BI boundary and peak toward the metallic region.

FIG. 3. Real-frequency results in the superconducting state at U = 12 and δ = 0.02 for t⊥= 1.0, 1.62 (≃t⊥,c), and 2.0 (left to right). From top to bottom: spectral function Aγ(K, ω) (Γ-α: red, M-β: blue); anomalous self-energy Σano γ (K, ω) for Γ-α and then M-β (solid: Re Σano, dashed: Im Σano); and Im Xγ for Γ-α and then M-β with X ∈{Σnor, W, Σnor + W} (Im Σnor γ : dashed, Im Wγ: dash-dotted, sum: solid). Per- panel scale factors (except Aγ) are given in the upper-left corner. Black arrows mark the pole-to-pole cancellation be- tween Σnor γ and Wγ, derived analytically in Sec. S3.

FIG. 4. Hidden-fermion fit of Σnor γ (K, ω) (top) and Σano γ (K, ω) (bottom) at U = 12 and δ = 0.02: the M-β com- ponent at t⊥= 1.0 (left) and the Γ-α component at t⊥= 2.0 (right). Blue curves are the DCA data and red curves are the fitting with the hidden-fermion model [Eqs. (7) and (8)]; solid and dashed curves denote real and imaginary parts. A single low-energy hidden fermion reproduces the pole structure of both channels.
